data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's thesis that the independence/uncorrelated distinction is purely epistemological fails to supply a causal mechanism the problem demands. From a causal-model perspective, the distinction is ontological: two failure causes are independent iff their generating mechanisms are structurally disconnected (no shared causal ancestor in the true causal graph). Identifying a hidden common cause updates the model but doesn't erase the prior ontological fact that, in the actual generative process, either a shared cause existed or didn't. The target's mechanism conflates our discovery of correlation with the existence of a causal link, providing no criterion for distinguishing independent from uncorrelated failures beyond 'whatever the observer currently believes'.
